anchor.quote: people use a small number of predictive cues to place parties, though more politically sophisticated voters draw from a broader set of policies, values, and constituencies.

claims.note:
Fix: Footnote omits the authors; add "Seonghui Lee, Lie Philip Santoso, and Randolph Stevenson" and the subtitle.
Finding: The cited work exists and says precisely this. *Heuristic Inference and the Left-Right: An Experimental Analysis of How Voters Form Their Left-Right Images of Parties*, by Seonghui Lee, Lie Philip Santoso, and Randolph Stevenson, Cambridge Elements in Experimental Political Science, 2026 (online June 26, 2026). Conjoint experiments in Canada, Denmark, Germany, UK; voters infer party left-right positions from policy, value, partisan-cooperation, and social-group cues; less sophisticated voters lean on partisan signals, more sophisticated voters "draw from a broader range of indicators, including party policies, ideological values, and social group support."
claims.text: "Voters use them to infer large bundles of positions from a few cues… [^1]"; §VIII: "people use a small number of predictive cues to place parties, though more politically sophisticated voters draw from a broader set of policies, values, and constituencies."

anchor.quote: Ideologies draw from a common field of contested political concepts—liberty, equality, authority, community, democracy, order—and give them determinate meaning by placing them into characteristic configurations.[^2]

claims.note:
Fix: none required.
Finding: Accurate summary of Freeden's morphology: ideologies are configurations of contested concepts whose meanings are fixed by "decontestation" and by each concept's relations/position within the configuration (core/adjacent/peripheral). Both cited works exist at the cited URLs: the OUP page for *Ideologies and Political Theory: A Conceptual Approach* and the Oxford Handbook of Political Ideologies chapter "The Morphological Analysis of Ideology." Primary texts are paywalled; content verified via secondary.
claims.text: "Michael Freeden's morphological theory… Ideologies draw from a common field of contested political concepts—liberty, equality, authority, community, democracy, order—and give them determinate meaning by placing them into characteristic configurations.[^2]"

anchor.quote: parties can be classified by origin, organization, international affiliation, name, policy, or ideology, and the boundaries do not always coincide.[^3]

claims.note:
Fix: Drop "organization" or rephrase to track the four approaches ("origin, transnational affiliation, policy and ideology, or name").
Finding: Mair & Mudde 1998 identify **four** approaches: (1) origin and sociology, (2) international federations/transnational groupings, (3) policy and ideology, (4) party name. The draft's list is essentially right but interpolates "organization" as if it were a separate approach, and splits policy/ideology into two. Substance (boundaries don't coincide; origin and ideology best suited) is correct.
claims.text: "parties can be classified by origin, organization, international affiliation, name, policy, or ideology, and the boundaries do not always coincide.[^3]"

anchor.quote: economic and cultural attitudes can be separated both conceptually and empirically.[^4] Second, no universal factor structure settles politics once and for all.

claims.note:
Fix: none for accuracy; consider acknowledging that [^4]'s second source finds mass opinion weakly structured *tout court* (Phase 3 matter). Note: the first source is a 2-page open peer commentary — legitimate but lightweight for a T1 load-bearing footnote.
Finding: Both cited works exist and support the sentences as written. Feldman & Huddy argue "political ideology is best explained by at least two dimensions linked to economic and social ideology." Mongrain & Walgrave (EJPR 2026) find no single settled structure — indeed largely *non*-dimensional mass opinion in Belgium (elite constraint 2–3× citizens'). Caveat for Phase 3: the second source's central finding (mass publics show minimal ideological structure of any dimensionality) also cuts against a five-axis structure in mass opinion; the draft's hedged use ("no universal factor structure") is accurate but the source proves more than the draft acknowledges.

Finding: Author's own exploratory analysis; exact values depend on unstated variable choices, but the pattern **reproduces**. I downloaded CHES 2024 and built plausible composites (economy: lrecon/redistribution/deregulation/spendvtax; culture: galtan/womens_rights/lgbtq_rights/samesex_marriage/religious_principles; coercion: civlib_laworder/executive_power; belonging: nationalism/immigrate_policy/multiculturalism/ethnic_minorities; system: anti_elite_salience/people_v_elite). findings.body: Claim the ground the piece actually occupies. Its real contribution is not the five axes (four of which exist verbatim on a quiz site) but the *grammar* — the separation of coordinates from family names, and the usage discipline around them. Add the section that names your predecessors and flanking opponents (8values, GAL/TAN, Bobbio, Lewis & Lewis, Caplan) and answers "why five" as a pragmatic optimum between one line and issue-atomism. Every other major issue becomes easier once the piece knows which conversation it is in.
findings.title: The one thing

anchor.quote: The point is not that politics secretly has five axes

findings.body:
- **The problem:** §II's counterfactual-independence test overgenerates — ecology, foreign policy, centralization, and regime commitment all pass it, and §X concedes as much by exiling exactly those to "modules" with no stated selection principle. Meanwhile the discourse audit found the four non-System axes replicate the 8values test — *three with verbatim pole names* — and the strongest published counterargument (Lewis & Lewis, *The Myth of Left and Right*, 2023, sharpened in the Caplan–Lewis exchange) attacks precisely this joint: if bundling is the spectrum's sin, five axes is a bigger reification, since each "question" is itself a bundle (Economy compresses trade, tax, redistribution, regulation, property, labor — a protectionist tax-cutter has no true Economy score, only a lossy 3). The Lewises are simultaneously the nearest predecessor of §VIII's own "coalition names" thesis and its standing refutation; the piece neither credits nor answers them. Steelman considered: the draft's fragments (§VII "Labels gain explanatory power by excluding detail," the metadata, the modules) already imply the answer — five is a pragmatic optimum between one line and issue-atomism — but an implied answer to an unnamed objection is invisible.
- **Why it matters here:** The hostile-but-fair one-liner writes itself: "8values with a populism axis and no test, which never says why five." For an AI-adjacent readership primed to detect derivative taxonomy, the unnamed 8values overlap alone is disqualifying if a reader finds it before you disclose it.
- **Direction:** Add one section (or two long paragraphs) — "Why five, and not fifty" — that (a) gives the genealogy in one paragraph: Nolan → Political Compass → 8values → 9Axes, crediting 8values by name and explaining why a *test* is the wrong form (tests score people; this vocabulary describes claims); (b) names Caplan's pragmatic monism and Lewis eliminativism as the flanking positions and locates the framework between them; (c) states the selection principle for core-vs-module (historical recurrence across polities and centuries; coalition-forming power; mutual irreducibility) and applies it visibly to Green and foreign policy.
findings.title: The central number is never argued, and the predecessors who make that fatal are never named

anchor.quote: Culture, coercion, and belonging formed a strong contemporary bundle, correlating at roughly .78 to .82

findings.body:
- **The problem:** Heads-I-win framing — near-orthogonal composites would also have "confirmed" the framework ("distinct enough to separate; history binds them"). Worse, the bundle *is* GAL/TAN: the Chapel Hill survey was built around the Hooghe–Marks two-dimensional model whose second dimension welds green/alternative/libertarian to traditionalism/authority/nationalism, and Kitschelt's diagonal is the standard published explanation for the bundling the draft attributes to "history." A political scientist reads §II as naive rediscovery; the ledger meanwhile confirms your correlations are real and reproducible (C10: .84–.90 / .47–.56 / −.10 to −.20 on my re-derivation), so the empirics deserve better framing than they get. Also unstated: which variables entered each composite — the exercise is currently irreproducible as described.
- **Why it matters here:** §II is the piece's only empirical footing; as framed it is the piece's most attackable section for exactly the readers it should impress.
- **Direction:** Cite GAL/TAN and Kitschelt; invert the framing — *the reigning two-dimensional model welds together three questions that current politics is visibly unwelding*, with Milei and welfare nationalism as the unwelding evidence; state what would count against the framework (if no consequential actors occupied the off-diagonal cells, the extra axes would be idle); and list the composite variables in an endnote so the exercise is checkable.
findings.title: The CHES exercise rediscovers its own dataset's design dimension and is framed unfalsifiably

anchor.quote: ## V. Coordinates Before Categories

findings.body:
- **The problem:** Nothing at the venue looks like the second half; the second read independently called it "two documents in a trench coat" and located the reader's death in the fourteen consecutive dictionary entries of §VI. The package already contains `taxonomy_reference_sheet.md` — the manual has a home that is not the essay's body. In the July-2026 environment, tables and symmetrical bulleted apparatus are also the surface features an AI-literate readership pattern-matches to machine-generated taxonomy — a reception risk the discourse report rates as the largest formal one.
- **Why it matters here:** This is the venue's first politics piece; it will be judged as an essay, and the essay is currently interrupted for roughly 2,500 words.
- **Direction:** Keep the *argument* of the apparatus, compress the *inventory*. §VI: discuss the families that do argumentative work (socdem/demsoc as a minimal pair; welfare nationalist and natcon as the proof that left/right fails; libertarian via Milei) in continuous prose and hand the rest to the figure and the linked reference sheet. §X: two paragraphs (the trust argument + regime type as the non-negotiable tag). §XI: keep Rule 5 and the charitable-poles material as prose, fold rules 1–4 and 6 into a paragraph or the reference sheet. Cut the 1–5 scale table; state it in a sentence.
findings.title: Essay and manual in a trench coat — a genre break the venue cannot absorb

anchor.quote: Orbán is a welfare nationalist

findings.body:
- **The problem:** Ledger C23a: the mid-2026 record is tariff-centered and state-directive (universal §122 baseline tariff after the February IEEPA ruling; §232 tariffs of 10–50% across major sectors; applied rate ≈ 11.8%; a 9.9% federal Intel stake; a sovereign wealth fund) — "market-leaning" as the first coordinate misleads on the draft's own Economy axis, and §V itself warns that "a nominally market-oriented party can construct protectionist policy." Ledger C23d: Orbán lost power on April 12, 2026 (Tisza supermajority) — the present tense is false in a draft that postdates it (it cites a June 10 Pew report), an ironic breach of the draft's own Rule 4, "date every profile." More generally (second read Objection 3, adopted): the profiles carry no dates, no evidence, no rhetoric/program/practice split, and the essay never once runs its machinery end-to-end on a contested case — its flagship application is scored on exactly the vibes Rule 1 ranks last.
- **Why it matters here:** "Trump: market-leaning" is the single most screenshot-quotable phrase in the piece for hostile readers, and both errors are self-inflicted demonstrations of the framework's necessity.
- **Direction:** Convert both bugs into features. Trump becomes the worked demonstration of the rhetoric/program/practice split ("market-rhetorical, protectionist-statist in practice"), with dates and two cited facts. Orbán's profile is dated ("in office 2010–2026") and his fall becomes live evidence in the insurgent/institutional discussion. Add one sentence before the profiles conceding they are dated, disputable illustrations of the grammar, not verdicts.
findings.title: The showcase profiles violate the essay's own rules — including two Misleading-in-context findings on named persons

anchor.quote: ## IV. What Populism Contains

findings.body:
- **The problem:** Müller's exclusive-moral-representation thesis is the unnamed source of the "moral dualism"/"unitarism"/pluralism facets, currently presented as an unpacking of Mudde; Akkerman–Mudde–Zaslove and POPPA show disaggregated populism measurement is existing practice, so the facets are a design choice among known components, not a discovery; "Welfare Nationalist" renames welfare chauvinism (Andersen & Bjørklund 1990, thirty years of literature); prototype-family semantics ≈ Collier & Mahon's radial categories (1993). None of this destroys the section's originality — the two-level architecture and the three-way disambiguation remain yours — but unacknowledged, each is a "reinvented X" tweet waiting to be written.

findings.body: Section XI, Rule 1 orders evidence from "enacted policy and governing practice" down to "isolated quotations, vibes, and cultural association," and Section V insists every address carry salience, confidence, time, and object metadata ("These distinctions are not bureaucratic ornament"). Yet the essay's own demonstration cases — Section VII's "Trump is a populist natcon: market-leaning, authority-oriented, culturally traditional, strongly communal, and insurgent, with unitary and personalist features," and the parallel Obama, Milei, and Orbán sentences — are delivered with no evidence, no dates, no object specification, and no rhetoric/program/practice split, despite Section V having just argued that a leader "can campaign as an insurgent, govern through institutions, and use unitary rhetoric." (Is "market-leaning" Trump the 2017 tax-cut president or the tariff president the opening paragraph invokes against Milei?) The framework's flagship application is scored on exactly the vibes its own Rule 1 ranks last. Relatedly, the essay never once runs its machinery on a live, contested disagreement end-to-end; Section XII's improved sentences are substitutions, not demonstrations. The single most persuasive thing this piece could contain — one real dispute, scored with cited evidence, yielding a non-obvious conclusion — is absent.

findings.body: The Nolan chart, the Political Compass, GAL/TAN, 8values-style quizzes, and Pew's typologies all already decompose left–right into multiple dimensions; several have decades of public circulation and none has displaced the spectrum. The essay engages none of them as *predecessors* (Pew appears in Section IX only as a foil for historical contingency) and so never answers the obvious question: why will this scheme succeed where they failed? The problem is sharpened by the essay's own best section. Section VIII argues that left–right "persist[s] because they solve a real coordination problem... A one-word cue compresses policies, values, social groups, historical loyalties, and expectations about alliance." That is an adoption argument *against* a five-number address with four metadata fields and three profiles per actor. "It should sit beneath it" (Section VIII) gestures at an answer — the vocabulary is for analysts and writers, not voters — but the intended user is never specified, and Section XIII's "We do not need a more complicated compass. We need a grammar" is an aphorism doing the work of an argument.
findings.title: The essay never confronts the graveyard of previous compasses, and its own Section VIII explains why it may join them

findings.body: Concrete instances: (a) Footnote 1 — "*Heuristic Inference and the Left-Right*, Cambridge University Press, 2026" — cites a work with no author, twice load-bearing (Sections "intro" and VIII). (b) Section VI, Socdem entry: "less committed to replacing capitalism than the democ" — "democ" is a typo or a ghost of an abandoned coinage; either way it is a defined-term failure in the very lexicon the essay is proposing. (c) The figures are referenced out of order: figure_5 appears in Section V, figure_4 in Section VI. (d) Footnote 8 cites Mudde's thin-centered definition via a university lecture page rather than the canonical published statements (e.g., "The Populist Zeitgeist," *Government and Opposition*, 2004, or Mudde & Rovira Kaltwasser). (e) The 2024 CHES figure of "609 political scientists... 279 European parties" and the June 2026 Pew typology names are stated with precision that must be verified against the sources before publication; I could not verify them on this read and they are exactly the kind of detail hostile readers check first. For a piece whose thesis is disciplined precision of vocabulary, apparatus sloppiness is not cosmetic — it is on-theme damage.

paragraphs: **Major revisions.** This is a serious, intelligent, unusually honest piece of conceptual construction whose factual substrate is close to impeccable — the fact-check came back cleaner than any draft of this ambition I have seen (zero contradicted claims; your own statistical exercise *reproduces from the raw data*). It is not yet publishable, for three structural reasons, none cosmetic: it never argues for its central number or names the predecessors that make that omission fatal; its empirical showpiece rediscovers the design dimension of its own dataset and frames the result unfalsifiably; and it is two documents in a trench coat — an essay and a user manual — at a venue that publishes only essays. The independent second read, given nothing but the draft, reached the same verdict for substantially the same reasons, which should give you confidence that these are properties of the text, not of one reader.

**The one thing:** Claim the ground the piece actually occupies. Its real contribution is not the five axes (four of which exist verbatim on a quiz site) but the *grammar* — the separation of coordinates from family names, and the usage discipline around them. Add the section that names your predecessors and flanking opponents (8values, GAL/TAN, Bobbio, Lewis & Lewis, Caplan) and answers "why five" as a pragmatic optimum between one line and issue-atomism. Every other major issue becomes easier once the piece knows which conversation it is in.
letterSections.title: Verdict

paragraphs: The left–right spectrum is a lossy compression of at least five recurrent, analytically separable political disagreements — over economy, coercion, culture, belonging, and the mediation of political will. The error is not the compression but mistaking it for the thing compressed. The remedy is a three-layer public vocabulary: five-axis coordinates that describe positions exactly; a disciplined lexicon of prototype family names (socdem, natcon, welfare nationalist…) that identify historical neighborhoods speakably; and modifiers, metadata, and regime tags for what both miss — with left and right retained *above* the coordinates as coalition names, doing the coordination work they have always done. Success, on the piece's own terms, is a reader who stops arguing about five different things while pretending there is only one.

That is a real project, and the second read reconstructed the same thesis independently — the draft transmits it reliably. The audience is the venue's: educated generalists fluent in the history of ideas, primed by seven prior essays of continuous Bourdieu-inflected prose about AI and modernity. This would be the publication's first politics piece — a genre debut that raises, rather than lowers, the bar for formal control.

paragraphs: ### 1. The central number is never argued, and the predecessors who make that fatal are never named

- **Where:** The title; §II ("The point is not that politics secretly has five axes…"); §X's module exclusions; the entire absence of 8values, Lewis & Lewis, Nolan/Political Compass from a piece about multi-axis political vocabularies.
- **The problem:** §II's counterfactual-independence test overgenerates — ecology, foreign policy, centralization, and regime commitment all pass it, and §X concedes as much by exiling exactly those to "modules" with no stated selection principle. Meanwhile the discourse audit found the four non-System axes replicate the 8values test — *three with verbatim pole names* — and the strongest published counterargument (Lewis & Lewis, *The Myth of Left and Right*, 2023, sharpened in the Caplan–Lewis exchange) attacks precisely this joint: if bundling is the spectrum's sin, five axes is a bigger reification, since each "question" is itself a bundle (Economy compresses trade, tax, redistribution, regulation, property, labor — a protectionist tax-cutter has no true Economy score, only a lossy 3). The Lewises are simultaneously the nearest predecessor of §VIII's own "coalition names" thesis and its standing refutation; the piece neither credits nor answers them. Steelman considered: the draft's fragments (§VII "Labels gain explanatory power by excluding detail," the metadata, the modules) already imply the answer — five is a pragmatic optimum between one line and issue-atomism — but an implied answer to an unnamed objection is invisible.
- **Why it matters here:** The hostile-but-fair one-liner writes itself: "8values with a populism axis and no test, which never says why five." For an AI-adjacent readership primed to detect derivative taxonomy, the unnamed 8values overlap alone is disqualifying if a reader finds it before you disclose it.
- **Direction:** Add one section (or two long paragraphs) — "Why five, and not fifty" — that (a) gives the genealogy in one paragraph: Nolan → Political Compass → 8values → 9Axes, crediting 8values by name and explaining why a *test* is the wrong form (tests score people; this vocabulary describes claims); (b) names Caplan's pragmatic monism and Lewis eliminativism as the flanking positions and locates the framework between them; (c) states the selection principle for core-vs-module (historical recurrence across polities and centuries; coalition-forming power; mutual irreducibility) and applies it visibly to Green and foreign policy.
### 2. The CHES exercise rediscovers its own dataset's design dimension and is framed unfalsifiably

- **Where:** §II: "Culture, coercion, and belonging formed a strong contemporary bundle, correlating at roughly .78 to .82… This is exactly what the framework should predict."
- **The problem:** Heads-I-win framing — near-orthogonal composites would also have "confirmed" the framework ("distinct enough to separate; history binds them"). Worse, the bundle *is* GAL/TAN: the Chapel Hill survey was built around the Hooghe–Marks two-dimensional model whose second dimension welds green/alternative/libertarian to traditionalism/authority/nationalism, and Kitschelt's diagonal is the standard published explanation for the bundling the draft attributes to "history." A political scientist reads §II as naive rediscovery; the ledger meanwhile confirms your correlations are real and reproducible (C10: .84–.90 / .47–.56 / −.10 to −.20 on my re-derivation), so the empirics deserve better framing than they get. Also unstated: which variables entered each composite — the exercise is currently irreproducible as described.
- **Why it matters here:** §II is the piece's only empirical footing; as framed it is the piece's most attackable section for exactly the readers it should impress.
- **Direction:** Cite GAL/TAN and Kitschelt; invert the framing — *the reigning two-dimensional model welds together three questions that current politics is visibly unwelding*, with Milei and welfare nationalism as the unwelding evidence; state what would count against the framework (if no consequential actors occupied the off-diagonal cells, the extra axes would be idle); and list the composite variables in an endnote so the exercise is checkable.
### 3. Essay and manual in a trench coat — a genre break the venue cannot absorb

- **Where:** The seam at §V. §§I–IV, VIII–IX, XII–XIII are an essay; §§V–VII, X–XI are a reference manual (scoring table, metadata checklist, 14-entry glossary, 9 modifiers, 6 exclusion subsections, 7 rules).
- **The problem:** Nothing at the venue looks like the second half; the second read independently called it "two documents in a trench coat" and located the reader's death in the fourteen consecutive dictionary entries of §VI. The package already contains `taxonomy_reference_sheet.md` — the manual has a home that is not the essay's body. In the July-2026 environment, tables and symmetrical bulleted apparatus are also the surface features an AI-literate readership pattern-matches to machine-generated taxonomy — a reception risk the discourse report rates as the largest formal one.
- **Why it matters here:** This is the venue's first politics piece; it will be judged as an essay, and the essay is currently interrupted for roughly 2,500 words.
- **Direction:** Keep the *argument* of the apparatus, compress the *inventory*. §VI: discuss the families that do argumentative work (socdem/demsoc as a minimal pair; welfare nationalist and natcon as the proof that left/right fails; libertarian via Milei) in continuous prose and hand the rest to the figure and the linked reference sheet. §X: two paragraphs (the trust argument + regime type as the non-negotiable tag). §XI: keep Rule 5 and the charitable-poles material as prose, fold rules 1–4 and 6 into a paragraph or the reference sheet. Cut the 1–5 scale table; state it in a sentence.
### 4. The showcase profiles violate the essay's own rules — including two Misleading-in-context findings on named persons

- **Where:** §VII: "Trump is a populist natcon: **market-leaning**…" and "Orbán is a welfare nationalist: … **populist in legitimation despite governing through a consolidated institutional apparatus**."
- **The problem:** Ledger C23a: the mid-2026 record is tariff-centered and state-directive (universal §122 baseline tariff after the February IEEPA ruling; §232 tariffs of 10–50% across major sectors; applied rate ≈ 11.8%; a 9.9% federal Intel stake; a sovereign wealth fund) — "market-leaning" as the first coordinate misleads on the draft's own Economy axis, and §V itself warns that "a nominally market-oriented party can construct protectionist policy." Ledger C23d: Orbán lost power on April 12, 2026 (Tisza supermajority) — the present tense is false in a draft that postdates it (it cites a June 10 Pew report), an ironic breach of the draft's own Rule 4, "date every profile." More generally (second read Objection 3, adopted): the profiles carry no dates, no evidence, no rhetoric/program/practice split, and the essay never once runs its machinery end-to-end on a contested case — its flagship application is scored on exactly the vibes Rule 1 ranks last.
- **Why it matters here:** "Trump: market-leaning" is the single most screenshot-quotable phrase in the piece for hostile readers, and both errors are self-inflicted demonstrations of the framework's necessity.
- **Direction:** Convert both bugs into features. Trump becomes the worked demonstration of the rhetoric/program/practice split ("market-rhetorical, protectionist-statist in practice"), with dates and two cited facts. Orbán's profile is dated ("in office 2010–2026") and his fall becomes live evidence in the insurgent/institutional discussion. Add one sentence before the profiles conceding they are dated, disputable illustrations of the grammar, not verdicts.

- **Where:** §IV (facets), §VI (Welfare Nationalist), §I/§VI (prototype semantics), §III.4 (Belonging).
- **The problem:** Müller's exclusive-moral-representation thesis is the unnamed source of the "moral dualism"/"unitarism"/pluralism facets, currently presented as an unpacking of Mudde; Akkerman–Mudde–Zaslove and POPPA show disaggregated populism measurement is existing practice, so the facets are a design choice among known components, not a discovery; "Welfare Nationalist" renames welfare chauvinism (Andersen & Bjørklund 1990, thirty years of literature); prototype-family semantics ≈ Collier & Mahon's radial categories (1993). - **Direction:** One clause or endnote each. Müller in the §IV text proper (he is the best-known populism author among your likely readers); the others can live in the endnotes.
### 6. Only the beatable defense of left–right is engaged

- **Why it matters here:** The philosophy-literate audience is precisely the one that knows Bobbio and Freeden.

letterSections.title: Fact-check summary

paragraphs: The piece enters a conversation far more crowded than its reference list admits (full map in `02-discourse-report.md`). The popular multi-axis tradition (Nolan 1969 → Political Compass → 8values → 9Axes/PolitiScales) has run the "spectrum conflates separable disagreements" argument for fifty years; 8values shares four axes with the draft, three with verbatim pole names, and even a crude coordinates-then-nearest-family mechanic. Academically, GAL/TAN is the draft's culture-coercion-belonging bundle; welfare chauvinism is its Welfare Nationalist; Müller/Akkerman et al. are its System facets; Lewis & Lewis published its "coalition names" thesis in 2023.

**Originality verdict: novel synthesis with significant unwitting reinventions — currently packaged to advertise the reinvented layer.** Against interest: the discourse audit found *no prior work anywhere* combining (a) the explicit coordinates-vs-names two-function separation, (b) a disciplined prototype lexicon with modifiers, and (c) usage rules (metadata, rhetoric/program/practice, no-master-score, evidence hierarchy). The grammar is new. The axes are not. The revision should invert the advertising accordingly.
**Strongest existing counterargument:** Lewis & Lewis's granularity/anti-reification argument (Major issue 1). The draft is partially armored by accident; it must armor itself on purpose.
letterSections.title: The discursive situation

paragraphs: Publication day, realistically: the venue's readership is small, AI-focused, and formally attentive; this is its first politics piece. (1) Rationalist-adjacent readers are the likeliest sharers and the source of the deadliest one-liner ("8values with a populism axis and no test") — and also the natural adopters of the no-master-score rule and the three-layer profile sentences. (2) Political scientists will spot GAL/TAN, welfare chauvinism, and the irreproducible composites — or, post-revision, will respect a piece that names them. (3) Partisan readers will screenshot "market-leaning" Trump (fixed by Major issue 4) and contest Modi's natcon membership (defensible; keep the "not interchangeable" hedge and consider a Hindu-nationalism clause). Favorable quotables: the compression opening, "Left and right are coalition names," "never compute a master score," the §XII rewrites. Misreadings to preempt in text: that the axes are natural kinds (one-line reminder inside §III); that the charitable-poles table is both-sides moral equivalence (give the existing disclaimer one more sentence); that coordinates score *people* ("what's my number?" — the classify-arguments rule, stated earlier); that Insurgent = populist = bad (§IV's disambiguation, forward-referenced sooner).
letterSections.title: Reception forecast

paragraphs: Patterns with exemplars (full detail in `04-craft-notes.md`):

- **"Not X. It is Y." saturation** — ≥15 instances; a venue signature at 5, an AI-cadence liability at 15. Keep the intro's, §I's, §VI's prototype line, and the closing; recast the rest as positive assertions (e.g., "It is not a disguised measure of government size" → "A large welfare state can remain strongly civil-libertarian; a privatizing state can expand prisons and surveillance" already does the work — delete the drumbeat sentence and lead with the evidence).
- **Apparatus intrusions** — the 1–5 scale table, the §VII triple Q&A blockquotes, ~10 pull-quote emphasis blocks; halve, per Major issue 3.
- **Register drops** — §VI encyclopedia voice ("The term is short for democratic socialist…"), §XI style-guide imperatives ("Record which."); rewrite as essay prose where retained.
- **First person** — used exactly once ("I constructed exploratory composites"); correct venue calibration; keep singular.
letterSections.title: Line notes

paragraphs:
| Dimension | Score | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Thesis & contribution | 4 | Clear, contestable, transmitted (second read reconstructed it verbatim); packaging misallocates emphasis to the axes (03-A0), but the contribution is real. |
| Argument rigor | 3 | Capped: strongest counterargument (Lewis & Lewis) unengaged (Major issue 1); CHES framing unfalsifiable (MI 2); core §I/§IV reasoning is strong. |
| Evidence & accuracy | 2 | Capped by rule: two Misleading-in-context Tier 1 findings (C23a, C23d) — despite an otherwise exceptional substrate (22 Verified, correlations reproduce). Both fixes are local; this is the cheapest two-point recovery in the piece. |
| Originality & situatedness | 2 | Four of five axes are an unwitting reinvention with verbatim pole names (8values); System facets ≈ existing measurement schemes; the piece does not know which conversation it is in — though the grammar layer is genuinely novel (discourse §2). |
| Structure | 2 | Essay/manual genre break at §V (MI 3); §VI pacing dead zone; convergent across both reads. |
| Prose | 4 | High control, venue-matched aphoristic register; liabilities are pattern-level (tic density, apparatus intrusions), not sentence-level. |
| Voice & audience fit | 3 | The essay half is the venue's voice; the manual half breaks it; the addressee of the vocabulary is never stated (03-A5). |
| Intellectual honesty | 3 | Unusually honest self-audit (§II, §X) — but "exactly what the framework should predict" overclaims, the profiles assert what the rules forbid, and §VIII wins the left/right debate by omission of Bobbio. |

**Lowest dimensions.** *Evidence & accuracy (2)* is a rule-cap, not a substrate judgment: fix the two §VII profiles (MI 4) and this is a 4 — no other change in the piece buys two points this cheaply. *Originality & situatedness (2)* and *Structure (2)* are the real work: one point on originality requires the positioning section (MI 1) plus the attribution clauses (MI 5); one point on structure requires the manual compression (MI 3).
letterSections.title: Scorecard

paragraphs:
1. **Structural surgery first.** Compress §VI to prose around 4–5 working families + reference-sheet handoff; reduce §X to two paragraphs; fold §XI rules 1–4/6 into prose, keep Rule 5 + charitable poles; cut the scale table and the Q&A blocks; resequence so the CHES material follows the five questions (§II's disclaimer folds into the presentation); fix figure order.
2. **Argument repairs, in dependency order.** (a) Write "Why five, and not fifty" — genealogy (8values credited), Caplan/Lewis flanks, selection principle (MI 1); (b) reframe CHES as the GAL/TAN-unwelding argument + falsifiability sentence + composite-variables endnote (MI 2); (c) rebuild the §VII profiles — Trump as the worked rhetoric/program/practice demonstration, Orbán dated 2010–2026, illustrative-not-verdict sentence (MI 4); (d) add Bobbio paragraph to §VIII and the Freeden-reflexivity sentence (MI 6); (e) attribution clauses: Müller in text, welfare chauvinism/Akkerman/Collier–Mahon in endnotes (MI 5); (f) one paragraph naming the addressee (discourse producers, trickle-down via [1]'s own mechanism).
3. **Research follow-ups** (starting sources, all fetched this session — URLs in dossier): 8values (https://8values.github.io/); Caplan–Lewis exchange (https://www.betonit.ai/p/the-myth-of-left-and-right-the-last); Hooghe–Marks–Wilson 2002 PDF (garymarks.web.unc.edu); Gonzalez's Bobbio-style reply (heterodoxacademy.org); Müller via LSE review; Tax Foundation tariff tracker (taxfoundation.org/research/all/federal/trump-tariffs-trade-war/); Al Jazeera on the April 12 Hungarian election.
4. **Craft passes** once structure is stable: ration the "not X / it is Y" cadence to ~5; kill register drops in retained apparatus; halve pull-quotes; add figure captions (CHES caveat in-caption); notation to interpuncts; convert citations to `[n]` endnotes with authors added ([1] Lee/Santoso/Stevenson; [8] + Mudde 2004), renumbered by first appearance.
5. **Open questions for the author.** (a) Modi in the natcon list: defensible with the hedge, but decide whether one clause on Hindu-nationalist specificity is worth the length. (b) The Green module: keep as-is or use it as the worked example of the selection principle (recommended — it converts a concession into a demonstration). (c) Whether to link the reference sheet publicly (recommended: it absorbs the manual). (d) Title: "Politics Has Five Questions" advertises the axes; something like "The Grammar of Political Disagreement" advertises the contribution — but the current title is stickier. Editor's lean: keep the title, fix the advertising in the text.
letterSections.title: Revision roadmap

paragraphs:
- **Second read, Objection 3 (full version): replace the four §VII profiles with a single worked case.** Adapted, not adopted: the four one-sentence profiles are the piece's most quotable payoff; instead, Trump's expands into the worked demonstration and all four get dates and an illustrative-not-verdict frame. Reason: the profiles are load-bearing for §XII's grammar demonstration and for reader adoption.
- **Reframing the piece as a reply to Lewis & Lewis throughout.** Rejected: one section suffices; a debate frame would surrender the piece's constructive register, which is its venue fit.
- **Cutting the CHES exercise entirely** (tempting given MI 2): rejected — the correlations reproduce, and the reframed version (unwelding GAL/TAN) is the piece's best answer to the parsimony objection. The empirics stay; the framing changes.
- **Retitling.** Considered (see open question d); the editor's lean is to keep it, so it is recorded here rather than as an issue.

Capped by rule: two Misleading-in-context Tier 1 findings (C23a, C23d) — despite an otherwise exceptional substrate (22 Verified, correlations reproduce). Both fixes are local; this is the cheapest two-point recovery in the piece.

delivered.verdict: **Major revisions.** This is a serious, intelligent, unusually honest piece of conceptual construction whose factual substrate is close to impeccable — the fact-check came back cleaner than any draft of this ambition I have seen (zero contradicted claims; your own statistical exercise *reproduces from the raw data*). It is not yet publishable, for three structural reasons, none cosmetic: it never argues for its central number or names the predecessors that make that omission fatal; its empirical showpiece rediscovers the design dimension of its own dataset and frames the result unfalsifiably; and it is two documents in a trench coat — an essay and a user manual — at a venue that publishes only essays. The independent second read, given nothing but the draft, reached the same verdict for substantially the same reasons, which should give you confidence that these are properties of the text, not of one reader.
